text: Several diseases cause nervous system signs (twisted neck, drooping wings, paralysis, blindness). Marek's disease (a viral avian cancer): tumors in different organs cause varied signs — the classic form attacks peripheral nerves, causing wing/leg paralysis; tumors in the eye cause irregular pupils and blindness; tumors in the liver/spleen/muscle in the acute form cause rapid death from massive internal tumors; a skin form develops in feather follicles, causing typical skin lesions and shedding large amounts of virus, making it the most infectious form. At necropsy, tumors cause nodular or diffuse organ enlargement, and in the classical form nerves can thicken 3–4 times normal size. Young chicks are most susceptible; hatchery vaccination prevents tumor formation but not infection itself. Newcastle Disease: some strains damage the nervous system, with nervous signs (twisted head/neck, circling, difficulty walking) generally following respiratory signs. Avian Encephalomyelitis: viral, affects chicks infected via the egg, starting right after hatching — dull-eyed expression, progressive incoordination, sitting on the hocks, head/neck tremors (especially when excited), and in advanced cases chicks lying with both feet to one side before dying; mortality varies by outbreak. Botulism (flaccid paralysis): a toxin from Clostridium bacteria, picked up from decaying carcasses, wet litter, other decaying organic matter, or fly maggots feeding on it — not spread bird-to-bird; causes flaccid paralysis of legs, wings, neck, and eyelids, progressing to a deep coma with the neck/head extended forward; prevention is prompt incineration/burial of dead birds and fly control.
